([[Katy, Texas]]) | college = *[[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]] (2020–2023) *[[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston]] (2023–2025) | draft_year = 2025 | career_start = 2025 | years1 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025]] | team1 = [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] | team2 = [[Golden State Warriors]] | years2 = {{nbay|2025|start}}–present | team3 = →Santa Cruz Warriors | years3 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025]]–present | highlights = * [[List of NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Champions|NCAA champion]] ([[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2021]]) * Third-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] – [[Associated Press|AP]], [[United States Basketball Writers Association|USBWA]], [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]], [[Sporting News|SN]] ([[2025 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2025]]) * First-team [[List of All-Big 12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big 12]] (2025) * Second-team All-Big 12 (2024) * Third-team All-Big 12 (2023) }} '''Lionel "LJ" Cryer Jr.''' (born October 9, 2001) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Golden State Warriors]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor Bears]] and [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston Cougars]]. ==High school career== Cryer played basketball for [[Morton Ranch High School]] in [[Katy, Texas]].{{cite web |last1=Silva II |first1=Dennis |title=One of a Kind |url=https://katytimes.com/stories/one-of-a-kind,1023? |website=[[Katy Times]] |access-date=November 21, 2021 |date=February 23, 2020}} As a junior, he averaged 27.5 points, 5.8 assists, and 2.9 rebounds per game, earning District 19-6A MVP honors.{{cite web |last1=Coleman |first1=Adam |title=Morton Ranch guard L.J. Cryer commits to Baylor |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/highschool/article/Morton-Ranch-guard-L-J-Cryer-commits-to-Baylor-13970020.php |website=[[Houston Chronicle]] |access-date=November 21, 2021 |date=June 11, 2019}} In the regular season finale of his senior season, Cryer had a 50-point, 10-assist game against [[Mayde Creek High School]]. In his senior season, Cryer averaged 34.2 points, 5.3 assists, 2.6 rebounds and 2.4 steals per game. He finished with 3,488 career points, the most in [[Houston]] area public school history. Cryer was selected as All-[[Greater Houston]] Player of the Year by the ''[[Houston Chronicle]]'', and repeated as District 19-6A MVP.{{cite web |last1=Coleman |first1=Adam |title=All-Greater Houston boys basketball player of year: LJ Cryer |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/highschool/article/AGH-boys-basketball-player-of-year-LJ-Cryer-15174937.php |website=[[Houston Chronicle]] |access-date=November 21, 2021 |date=April 2, 2020}}{{cite web |last1=Silva II |first1=Dennis |title=Morton Ranch's Cryer headlines all-district honorees |url=https://katytimes.com/stories/morton-ranchs-cryer-headlines-all-district-honorees,1114 |website=[[Katy Times]] |access-date=November 21, 2021 |date=March 15, 2020}} A four-star recruit, he committed to playing college basketball for [[Baylor Bears men's basketball|Baylor]] over offers from [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston]], [[Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball|Colorado]], [[LSU Tigers basketball|LSU]], [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]] and [[Stephen F. Austin Lumberjacks basketball|Stephen F. Austin]], among others. ==College career== Cryer received limited playing time as a freshman at Baylor, averaging 3.4 points per game as his team won the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|national championship]].{{cite web |last1=Davis |first1=Seth |title=Baylor's path to back-to-back national championship exists, but a new set of stars will have to emerge |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2887982/2021/10/15/baylors-path-to-back-to-back-national-championship-exists-but-a-new-set-of-stars-will-have-to-emerge/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=November 21, 2021 |date=October 15, 2021}} On November 20, 2021, he scored 21 points in an 86–48 victory against [[Stanford Cardinal men's basketball|Stanford]].{{cite news |title=No. 9 Baylor runs away from Stanford in second half, wins 86–48 |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/baylor-bears/2021/11/20/no-9-baylor-runs-away-from-stanford-in-second-half-wins-86-48/ |access-date=November 21, 2021 |work=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 20, 2021}} On January 29, 2022, Cryer was ruled out after aggravating a right foot injury.{{cite news |last1=Werner |first1=John |title=Alabama giant killers knock off Bears, 87-78 |url=https://wacotrib.com/sports/college/baylor/alabama-giant-killers-knock-off-bears-87-78/article_eda5047c-8168-11ec-9b93-a37d5d9266ba.html |access-date=February 15, 2022 |work=[[Waco Tribune-Herald]] |date=January 29, 2022}} He averaged 13.5 points, 1.7 assists and 1.5 rebounds per game.{{cite news |title=Baylor guard LJ Cryer to miss tournament's first weekend |url=https://sportsnaut.com/baylor-g-lj-cryer-to-miss-tournaments-first-weekend/ |access-date=March 6, 2023 |work=Sportsnaut |date=March 16, 2022}} As a junior, Cryer was named to the Third Team All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]].{{cite news |title=Flagler named first-team all-Big 12 |url=https://wacotrib.com/sports/college/baylor/flagler-named-first-team-all-big-12/article_99f8d02c-bba2-11ed-af41-6bdce25ad8ae.html |access-date=March 6, 2023 |work=[[Waco Tribune-Herald]] |date=March 5, 2023}} He averaged 15.0 points, 2.1 rebounds and 2.0 assists per game. Following the season, Cryer transferred to [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston]].{{cite news |last1=Vecenie |first1=Sam |title=Former Baylor guard LJ Cryer transferring to Houston: What it means for Cougars |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4395009/2023/04/09/lj-cryer-transfer-houston-baylor/ |access-date=April 14, 2026 |work=[[The Athletic]] |date=April 9, 2023}} He averaged 15.5 points, 2.4 rebounds, 1.9 assists, and 1.1 steals per game as a senior. Cryer was named to the Second Team All-Big 12. He decided to return for his fifth season of eligibility.{{cite news |last1=Gillenwater |first1=Sam |title=Houston guard LJ Cryer announces plans to return for 2024-25 season |url=https://www.on3.com/college/houston-cougars/news/houston-guard-lj-cryer-announces-plans-to-return-for-2024-25-season/ |access-date=April 14, 2026 |work=On3.com |date=April 9, 2024}} Cryer averaged 15.7 points, 2.4 rebounds and 2.0 assists per game. He helped the Cougars reach the NCAA championship game.{{cite news |last1=Borba |first1=Kevin |title=Former Houston Star LJ Cryer Recently Had Crazy 24 Hours |url=https://www.si.com/college/houston/basketball/former-houston-star-lj-cryer-recently-had-crazy-24-hours |access-date=April 14, 2026 |work=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=March 8, 2026}} ==Professional career== ===Golden State / Santa Cruz Warriors (2025–present)=== After going undrafted in the [[2025 NBA draft]], Cryer joined the [[Golden State Warriors]] for the [[2025 NBA Summer League]]. On June 27, 2025, he was signed to an [[Exhibit 10]] contract.https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/warriors-l-j-cryer-landing-with-golden-state/ Cryer was waived by the Warriors on October 18.https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-waive-guards-lj-cryer-seth-curry-20251018 For the [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025–26 season]], he was added to the training camp roster of the Warriors' [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]].{{cite news|title= Santa Cruz Warriors Announce 2025-26 Opening Night Roster |url= https://santacruz.gleague.nba.com/news/santa-cruz-warriors-announce-2025-26-opening-night-roster |access-date=November 7, 2025 |work=[[NBA G League]] |date=November 6, 2025}} Cryer signed a [[two-way contract]] with Golden State on December 2.{{Cite web |title=Warriors Sign Guard LJ Cryer to Two-Way Contract |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-sign-guard-lj-cryer-to-two-way-contract-20251202 |access-date=2025-12-02 |website=warriors.com |language=en}} On April 1, 2026, Cryer made his first career start, recording a career-high 17 points, one rebound, and three assists in a 127–113 loss to the [[2025–26 San Antonio Spurs season|San Antonio Spurs]].{{Cite web|title=Warriors' L.J. Cryer: Hits for 17 in first NBA start|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/warriors-lj-cryer-hits-for-17-in-first-nba-start/|access-date=April 11, 2026|website=cbssports.com|language=en}} On 2 July, 2026, he joined the Warriors for the [[2026 NBA Summer League]].{{Cite web|title= Warriors Announce Gold and Blue Rosters for California Classic |url= https://warriors.com/news/warriors-announce-gold-and-blue-rosters-for-california-classic-20260702 |website=NBA.com|date=July 2, 2026|access-date=July 2, 2026}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player
